task_message:
Case N38: segment the peripheral nerve sheath tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 261x261x396 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
Case N38 complete. 

**What was found:** A long, multinodular, T2-hyperintense serpiginous structure running along the course of the tibial nerve — from the popliteal region through the deep posterior compartment of the calf down to the distal third — consistent with a peripheral nerve sheath tumor (plexiform neurofibroma).

**How it was segmented:**
1. Located the lesion across axial/coronal/sagittal sheets: a "string of pearls" bright chain, the only conspicuous abnormality in the limb.
2. Seeded it with a point on the largest nodule (v1), then a positive scribble along the full length of the band in the sagittal plane (v2, 33.4 mL).
3. Added points on two missed nodules at the mid-calf level (v3, 55.5 mL), covering the chain from k≈94 to k≈330.
4. Reviewed the final 5-slice-per-plane panels: no lesion tissue beyond either end, outline tracks the bright tumor, and the single candidate correction (bone/vessel rim) was correctly rejected as normal tissue.

**Result:** 55.5 mL mask, 7 components (98.9% in the main lesion), saved with medium confidence — the boundary is clear, but the heterogeneous proximal segment and the small distal tail leave some residual uncertainty.
